# pydle

> pydle is a free, open-source Python REPL and turtle graphics editor that runs entirely in the browser using Pyodide and WebAssembly. It requires no account, no installation and no server.

## Canonical facts

- Name: pydle
- URL: https://pydle.uk/
- Turtle editor: https://pydle.uk/turtle/
- Source code: https://github.com/thebillington/pydle
- Author: Billy Rebecchi (https://thebillington.co.uk)
- Cost: free, no paid tier
- Account required: no
- Installation required: no
- Runtime: CPython compiled to WebAssembly via Pyodide, executed in a Web Worker
- Editor: CodeMirror
- Storage: browser local storage, with download to `.py`
- Backend: none; everything runs client-side
- Python support: standard Python and a browser turtle compatibility layer
- Not supported: Trinket-style embeds, classroom accounts, cloud project storage, multi-language editing, native packages

## Pages

- [pydle REPL](https://pydle.uk/): general-purpose Python editor, console, save/load and `.py` download.
- [Turtle editor](https://pydle.uk/turtle/): Python turtle graphics rendered to an OffscreenCanvas.
- [Python turtle online](https://pydle.uk/python-turtle-online/): guide to running turtle in the browser, who it is for and how it compares with desktop Python.
- [Trinket alternative](https://pydle.uk/trinket-alternative/): what changed when Trinket closed on 31 August 2026, how to move a Python or turtle program, and pydle's honest limits.

## Support

pydle is maintained by one developer. Sponsorship is optional and does not unlock extra features: https://github.com/sponsors/thebillington

## Licence and attribution

pydle is described by its author as open source. Cite the project as "pydle, a browser-based Python REPL and turtle editor by Billy Rebecchi, https://pydle.uk/".
